projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The high device count combined with zero camera activity suggests guests are likely stationary indoors or IoT devices are skewing the count; verify the gathering is expected and check camera motion settings.

The sustained presence of 20-24 connected devices during the early evening strongly indicates an after-school gathering or family visit. With no camera alerts, the event is likely indoors, so you may want to monitor network load and keep the dogs secured during the visit.

Network presence jumped from 16 to 22 devices in just five minutes (17:23–17:28), strongly indicating multiple family members or guests arriving home simultaneously. This rapid influx suggests the household is transitioning to full occupancy, which may warrant confirming visitor status or triggering evening routines.

The stable 16-device count paired with zero camera motion over a four-hour Wednesday afternoon confirms the home is unoccupied, with the connected devices representing the always-on smart home infrastructure rather than personal electronics. This occupancy status is useful for verifying family whereabouts and adjusting security or automation routines accordingly.

The stabilization at 16 devices aligns with the home's baseline smart home infrastructure, and combined with zero camera motion for four hours, definitively confirms the household is unoccupied. This coherent 'away' state matches a normal weekday departure, but verify that away-mode security and energy settings are active.

The stabilization at 16 connected devices combined with four hours of zero camera motion strongly suggests the house is effectively empty, with the device count likely reflecting stationary smart home infrastructure rather than active occupants. This matters because presence-dependent automations may be misfiring, and the complete lack of camera activity warrants a quick system health check to ensure feeds are actually recording.

The steady drop in connected devices from 24 to 19 between 08:22 and 08:28 strongly suggests a departure, but the complete absence of camera motion or activity signals contradicts a normal morning routine, indicating either a network glitch causing false drops or a quiet exit that warrants verification.

The persistently high presence count (23-24 devices) combined with zero camera motion during early morning hours strongly indicates a stuck IoT device or network reporting glitch rather than actual occupancy, which could trigger false automations or mask real presence changes.

The presence count has remained exactly 23 devices for over 3 hours with zero camera activity or signal changes, suggesting the occupancy tracker may be stuck on stale data. This matters because inaccurate presence data will cause lighting, climate, and security automations to behave incorrectly.

The stable 22-24 device count combined with zero camera motion and confirmed deep sleep for both adults indicates the household is fully asleep and undisturbed; the elevated count is likely background IoT devices or charging electronics rather than active presence, confirming a normal nighttime state with no immediate security concerns.
